title: Cloud Sensor Imaging-Window Alert
dataSources: Observatory environment (`observatory:env`), sky-quality meter (`skyquality:reading`), imaging sessions (`imaging:session`), telescope mount (`mount:status`), cloud sensor (`allsky:cloud`).
app: Backyard observatory automation — roll-off-roof/dome controller, sky-quality meter, cloud sensor, telescope mount, and astrophotography capture software (N.I.N.A./Ekos) — logging to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=allsky:cloud
| stats latest(sky_temp_c) as sky, latest(ambient_c) as amb
| eval spread=amb-sky, clear=if(spread>25,"clear","clouds")
description: Uses the sky-minus-ambient temperature spread to tell you when it is genuinely clear enough to open the observatory.
value: A cloud sensor protects both your gear and your sleep, opening only for real clear spells and closing before the clouds return.
implementation: Ingest an infrared cloud sensor into `index=personal`; alert when the sky clears enough for imaging.
visualization: Single-value clear-or-cloudy indicator with the temperature spread.
grandmaExplanation: It tells you when the sky is genuinely clear enough to set up the telescope, using a clever temperature trick.
